about.title: Galt Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Galt's economy leans on agriculture, trucking, and logistics operations spread along SR-99 and the industrial stretches near Twin Cities Road, which means workplace injuries here often involve forklifts, delivery vehicles, farm equipment, or falls on loading docks. California generally requires injured workers to go through workers' compensation rather than suing their employer directly, but that's not always the end of the story. When a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another company's driver contributed to your injury, you may have a separate claim outside the workers' comp system. LawProactive doesn't practice law or handle claims itself — we're a free connection service that matches injured Galt workers with an independent attorney who can sort out which path, or paths, apply to your situation. There's no cost to find out, and no obligation once you're connected. A quick conversation can clarify whether your case involves more than just a workers' comp filing.

whyChoose.title: Why Galt Workers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: We Help You See Past the Workers' Comp Wall
items.desc: Workers' comp is usually the exclusive remedy against an employer, but a negligent third party like a subcontractor or equipment maker can open a separate claim. We connect you with an attorney who can evaluate whether that applies to you.

items.title: Timing Matters and We Help You Move Fast
items.desc: You generally have 30 days to report a workplace injury to your employer, and any third-party claim carries a 2-year deadline. Getting matched with an attorney early helps protect both timelines.

items.title: Retaliation Protection Guidance
items.desc: California law prohibits employer retaliation for reporting a workplace injury. An independent attorney can help you understand your rights if you feel pressured after filing.

items.question: I was hurt driving a delivery route through Galt for my employer — is that just a workers' comp case?
items.answer: Not necessarily. If another driver, perhaps on SR-99 or Twin Cities Road, caused the collision, that driver's negligence could support a separate third-party claim alongside your workers' comp benefits. An independent attorney can review the details and let you know which claims apply.

items.question: What happens if my employer doesn't want me to report the injury?
items.answer: California law makes it illegal for an employer to retaliate against you for reporting a workplace injury, and you generally have 30 days to make that report. If you're facing pushback, an attorney connected through LawProactive can advise you on next steps.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No, the connection service is completely free, and attorneys in our network typically work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no upfront cost or obligation to move forward.
